source: Weekly Investment Meeting Summary, Monday 14 September 2026

headline.summary_title: Oil tops $100, the CPI locks in a hike
headline.intro_sentence: The S&P 500 lost 1.00% and no major index gained, but two prices did the work: Brent crossed $100 for the first time in four months, and the US 10-year pushed toward 5% as a hot core CPI made a September hike close to certain.

three_observations.headline: No index gained on the week
three_observations.body: Five of the six are lower over one month, yet all six are still up between 9.6% and 24.6% for the year.

three_observations.headline: The dispersion is in the sectors
three_observations.body: Energy is up 43.7% year to date while consumer discretionary is down 3.1% and utilities 0.9%.

three_observations.headline: Neither classic hedge worked
three_observations.body: Gold fell 1.5% and core bonds are negative again at -1.31%, munis worst of all, while crude gained 9.1%.

four_drivers.intro_sentence: Oil supply risk, a hot core CPI, a breakout at the long end of the curve and the midterm calendar. A macro week, not a micro one: earnings, AI capex and credit all stayed supportive.
four_drivers.policy_note: On the policy side: a 25 bps Fed hike is about 90% priced for Wednesday, the ECB has already hiked with a hawkish tone, and two BoE hikes by year end are 76% priced.

drivers.title: Energy supply risk
drivers.body: Drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, some 4 mb/d of bypass capacity, as Houthi forces completed control of Yemen's Red Sea coast. Hormuz is near 20% of pre-war capacity.

drivers.title: A hot core CPI
drivers.body: Headline prices rose 0.4% in August and core 0.3%, both above consensus, leaving annual inflation at 3.4%. Gasoline did the work, up 16.3% over the year, and producer prices added 5.4%.

drivers.title: The long end broke out
drivers.body: The 30-year added 8 bps to 5.37%, a fresh 19-year high, and the 2-year surged 16 bps to 4.59%, its largest one-day move since April 2025. The curve bear flattened.

drivers.title: The midterm calendar
drivers.body: Democrats' Senate odds rose to 56.6% from 51.1%, 52 days from the vote. The answer on offer, a $5,000 payment to every American adult, would cost $1.3 trillion. The bond market took it badly.

scenario.intro_sentence: The house baseline stays an Indian summer for 2026 at 50%, against a 30% inflation heatwave and a 20% growth freeze.

house_view.intro_sentence: Tactical asset allocation is unchanged since 21 August: neutral equities, underweight fixed income, overweight cash, gold and commodities, neutral hedge funds.

views.body: Micro is doing well and macro caps the upside. S&P 500 profits grew 50% in Q2 and analysts project 27% for Q3; within equities we combine AI-related and cyclical exposures.
The 10-year came within a hair of 5%, a level reached only once since 2007. A 10-year durably above 5% against a 5.3% earnings yield would remove the cushion under equities.
Gold and commodities stay overweight. EUR, CHF, GBP and EM currencies moved from underweight to neutral against the dollar, the yen already neutral.
